summary:
PATH KEY for citations: env.py / env_generator.py / problems/*.json = <scratchpad>\tampura_environments_full\tampura_environments\find_dice\...; panda_env_utils.py, robot.py, primitives.py, pb_utils.py, voxel_utils.py, grasping.py, precompute_grasps.py = ...\tampura_environments_full\tampura_environments\panda_utils\...; run_planner.py, find_dice.yml = ...\tampura_environments_full\{run_planner.py, env_configs\find_dice.yml}; environment.py, spec.py, structs.py, store.py, symbolic.py, policy.py, tampura_policy.py, random_policy.py, policies\__init__.py, policy_search.py, symk.py, mdp_solver.py, config.py = <git>\tampura\tampura\...; tampura_sweep.py, sweep_2026-05-26.json, seed_N.log = ...\scratchpad\wsl_tampura\{., ., sweep_consoles}.

WHAT find_dice IS. A wrist-camera, purely kinematic, belief-judged search-and-pick task. World: a 1.53 x 1.22 x 0.03 m table box at (0.1, 0, -0.015) plus four posts and four beams (only the table is an obstacle), a Franka Panda loaded from models/srl/franka_panda/panda.urdf with tool link panda_tool_tip and camera link camera_frame (640 x 480, fx = fy = 525, principal point (319.5, 239.5)). Objects are YCB meshes (trimesh visual, VHACD concave collision, pybullet default mass since mass=-1): one 'dice' plus 1 to 5 inverted cups from {a,b,c,d,e}_cups_ud. Scenes are NOT generated at run time: FindDiceEnv.get_scene_data does random.choice(os.listdir('tampura_environments/find_dice/problems')) over exactly three shipped JSONs (categories + poses). env_generator.py (offline tool) samples x ~ U(0.3, 0.7), y ~ U(-0.4, 0.4), yaw uniform, co-locates the die at the LAST placed cup's point (same xyz, identity quaternion) when a cup precedes it in the shuffled category order, rejects collisions and out-of-image poses, and saves only scenes whose home-pose segmentation mask does not contain the die's body id. Of the three scenes, two have the die exactly at a cup center at cup height (z 0.0493 and 0.0523: it floats, and never falls because nothing ever calls stepSimulation); the third (1747173590) has the die on the table (z 0.0209) 1.5 cm from d_cups_ud's center, hidden by chance. The global seed seeds random and np.random before env init and therefore controls scene choice, the grasp-library shuffle, look-conf and placement sampling, outcome sampling and MDP tie breaks. Observed seed-to-scene map from the console logs: 1747173590 <- seeds {1,2,3,4,8,14,15,18} (2/8 successes); 1747173591 (2 objects) <- {0,7,9,11,12,13,16} (6/7); 1747173593 <- {5,6,10,17,19} (3/5). os.listdir order is filesystem dependent, so the seed-to-scene map is reproducible only on the same tree; a seed-for-seed bridge must pin the scene file per seed from these logs.

OBSERVATION MODEL. Images come from the wrist camera at whatever arm configuration the robot is in (initial image at DEFAULT_ARM_POS). obs_from_camera_image returns, for every body id present in the segmentation mask, that body's TRUE pose read from world.poses: perfect detection and perfect pose, gated only by visibility. SceneBelief holds object_poses (known objects), a 15 mm VoxelGrid over x in [0.37, 0.815], y in [-0.61, 0.61] with two z layers (about 30 x 82 x 2 voxels), initially all occupied, meaning 'the die may be here'. update_visibility frees voxels whose center projects into the depth image with distance <= depth (include_unseen=True at init also frees voxels outside the image) and voxels within 7.5 mm of any KNOWN object's collision mesh. Voxels under an inverted cup survive (the cup top blocks the depth ray, the cavity is not within 7.5 mm of the walls): this is their containment hiding model, the die hypothesis is uniform over surviving voxels. Abstract belief atoms: known-pose(o), holding(o), at-grasp(o,g), is-target(die) (always present: the die's identity is known, only its pose is not), moved(o), at-home iff current_conf is allclose to DEFAULT_ARM_POS.

ACTIONS AND STREAMS. pick(?o,?g), place(?o,?g,?p), look(?o1,?o2,?q) ('look behind ?o2 for ?o1'), go-home() (only while holding), no-op. Streams are sampled ONCE per episode at t=0 (flat_sample true, flat_width 5): 5 grasps (GRASP_MODE 'saved': per-mesh JSON grasp library, shuffled), 5 placements (uniform on a shortened table, no collision check against other objects), 5 look confs (camera 20 to 30 cm above the object's pose at t=0 with 10 cm xy noise, pointed at it, IK via plan_workspace_motion with only the floor as obstacle) for every physical object including the die. look's effects_fn renders a depth image in the belief-side simulator and returns two abstract outcomes weighted (newly seen voxels) : (remaining occupied minus newly seen); the success branch puts the die at a random newly seen voxel. pick/place effects_fn succeed iff grasp_ik (IK + interpolated pregrasp-to-grasp path with collision checks) succeeds.

SUCCESS AND TERMINATION. reward = Exists o. is-target(o) and holding(o) and at-home, evaluated by eval_expr on the abstract BELIEF plus store.certified, never on the physical state. The sweep's success is rewards[-1] == 1.0. There is no early termination: Policy.rollout runs exactly max_steps = 20 steps, and once the reward is positive TampuraPolicy returns no-op (observation None, belief deep-copied). 'holding' enters the belief only through an observation whose grasp field is set, which pick_execute_fn does iff IK and the BiRRT plan succeed (no contact or lift check). go-home's observation carries conf = DEFAULT_ARM_POS even when its motion plan fails, so at-home can be believed without the arm moving.

EXECUTION (their Panda). plan_motion = BiRRT (restarts 1, iterations 20, smooth 100, 10 degree resolution) with a collision_fn against the floor and all environment bodies (self-collision on, 5 mm clearance). Execution is GroupTrajectory.iterate: with no GUI it TELEPORTS (set joint positions to the last waypoint); with a GUI it interpolates set_joint_positions with time.sleep(5e-3) per step. The held object follows the tool via Attachment.assign = resetBasePositionAndOrientation every iterate step; there is no createConstraint and no stepSimulation (sim_steps = 0). Consequences: a pick cannot physically fail, nothing ever falls, placements may interpenetrate, headless and GUI runs differ in wall time.

POLICY INTERFACE. Policy.rollout(env, b0, store) loops: a_b = b.abstract(store); reward; action, info, store = self.get_action(b, store); if no-op copy belief, else observation = env.step(action, b, store) which is schema.execute_fn(action, belief, env.state, store) -> (state, observation); bp = b.update(action, observation, store). A custom policy is a Policy subclass implementing get_action(belief, store) -> (Action(name, [store symbol strings]), info dict, store), registered with register_planner(name, cls) and selected by config 'planner: name'; it needs its own entry point because run_planner.py imports only tampura and tampura_environments. Exposed handles: belief.world (belief-side World: .client -> BulletClient, .robot.body, .objects body ids, .floor, .categories), env.state.world (real world), env.sim_world, env.starting_belief, store.get(sym) -> body id / Grasp / pose tuple / conf tuple; body ids are identical in both clients. Ground truth that leaks through those handles and must never be read by our bridge: the hidden die sits at its TRUE pose in the belief-side simulator (set_sim only moves KNOWN objects), so their look-conf sampling for ?o = die, their belief-side depth renders after cups move, and their collision checks all see it; and world.poses are true poses.

TIMING. RolloutHistory.time_deltas[i] = time.time() - st at the end of step i (cumulative since rollout start), covering get_action (flat stream sampling at t=0; 200 outcome samples per replan, each calling effects_fn, which does IK, BiRRT or a depth render in the belief simulator; SymK translate + search, about 20 ms) plus env.step execution. The local run: 11/20, loop_s 240 +/- 151 s over all episodes, 166 +/- 85 s over successes, wall adds about 12 s process startup; SymK totals 0.04 to 1.5 s per episode. Every inspected failure (seeds 1, 16, 18) is the same degeneracy: once a look that reveals zero voxels is chosen, F records a self-loop with probability 1, the envelope check (envelope_prob >= envelope_threshold = 1) suppresses replanning, and the MDP tie-break re-selects the same look until step 20.

facts.claim: Scene selection at run time is random.choice over os.listdir of the problems directory; exactly three problem JSONs are shipped (1747173590.312597, 1747173591.670785, 1747173593.826745). The only run-time rejection is the EXCLUDE_CLASSES filter (none of the cup classes or dice are excluded), so scenes are never regenerated or re-checked for hiddenness at run time.
facts.evidence: env.py:801-811 (get_scene_data), env.py:829-839 (while scene_data is None loop with EXCLUDE_CLASSES), panda_env_utils.py:63-77 (EXCLUDE_CLASSES), directory listing of problems/ (3 files)

facts.claim: env_generator.py is an offline tool: 1 to 5 cups from a_cups_ud..e_cups_ud plus 'dice', shuffled; poses x~U(0.3,0.7), y~U(-0.4,0.4), z = stable z on table + 0.01, yaw~U(-pi,pi); the die is co-located at the last placed cup's point (pose = Pose(cup_pose[0]), identity quaternion) only if a cup precedes it in the shuffled order; rejects pairwise collisions and poses whose point is outside the home-pose camera image; a scene is saved only if the die body id is absent from the home segmentation mask (MAX_ITER 20 placement tries, MAX_ATTEMPTS 20 scene tries).

Problem 1747173591.670785 has 2 objects [d_cups_ud, dice] at the identical point (0.6727, 0.2161, 0.0493); problem 1747173593.826745 has [a,d,e cups, dice, b cup] with the die at e_cups_ud's exact point (0.4863, -0.1584, 0.0523); problem 1747173590.312597 has [dice, b, e, d, a cups] with the die on the table at (0.5920, -0.2425, 0.0209), 1.5 cm from d_cups_ud at (0.5883, -0.2278, 0.0493). In two scenes the die therefore floats at cup-centre height.

Seed to scene map of the local 20-seed run (from 'Loading scene from' console lines): 1747173590 <- seeds 1,2,3,4,8,14,15,18; 1747173591 <- 0,7,9,11,12,13,16; 1747173593 <- 5,6,10,17,19. Successes per scene: 2/8, 6/7, 3/5 (total 11/20). seed_5 and seed_18 logs contain NUL bytes (seed 18 is two interleaved runs: a KeyboardInterrupt at t=0 followed by the resumed run), the JSON record is authoritative.
facts.evidence: seed_N.log:4 for N in 0..19; seed_18.log:8-62; sweep_2026-05-26.json:7-786; sweep_console_2026-05-26.full.log:3-27

facts.claim: run_planner.py seeds random and np.random with global_seed once, then env.initialize() (scene choice consumes random), then builds the policy and calls policy.rollout(env, b0, store). Config = yaml find_dice.yml updated by CLI args.

find_dice.yml: max_steps 20, batch_size 20, num_skeletons 10, flat_sample true, flat_width 5, pwa 0.2, pwk 3.0, envelope_threshold 1, num_samples 200, gamma 0.98, planner tampura_policy, learning_strategy bayes_optimistic, decision_strategy prob, symk unordered/fw/simple, from_scratch true, vis false.

The camera is wrist-mounted: Camera.get_pose reads the link pose of robot link 'camera_frame' and get_image renders from there (pbu.get_image_at_pose, far 5.0, segment=True). Intrinsics 640x480, fx=fy=525, cx=319.5, cy=239.5. There is no fixed external camera.

Observation = SceneObservation(camera_image, poses, grasp, grasp_body, conf, moved, possible_locations). obs_from_camera_image takes the unique body ids of segmentationMaskBuffer[:,:,0] and for each matching object symbol returns the TRUE pose from world.poses (pbu.get_pose). Detection and pose are perfect, gated only by visibility.

SceneBelief visibility grid: GRID_RESOLUTION 0.015; AABB x in [0.37, floor_upper_x - 0.05], y = full table width, z lower = table top + 0.02, z upper overridden to 0.03; grid origin offset z = 0.01; all voxels initially occupied. The grid is a belief over possible die locations, not an occupancy map.

update_visibility frees (a) voxels whose centre projects inside the image with camera-frame distance <= depth at that pixel (include_unseen=True at initialize also frees voxels outside the image), and (b) voxels within GRID_RESOLUTION/2 = 7.5 mm (getClosestPoints with a 1 mm sphere) of any KNOWN object's collision body. Voxels inside an inverted cup's cavity survive both tests: that is the containment hiding model.

Abstract belief = known-pose(o) for each o in object_poses; holding(o) and at-grasp(o,g) if grasp set; is-target(o) for every object whose category == 'dice' (always known); moved(o) per moved list; at-home iff current_conf allclose DEFAULT_ARM_POS (rtol/atol 1e-4).

Belief.update deep-copies, sets placed on 'place', appends observation.moved, sets current_conf = observation.conf, merges observation.poses into object_poses, calls set_sim (moves KNOWN objects in the belief-side simulator to belief poses; None poses are parked at x=100), updates visibility if a camera image is present, and sets grasp/grasp_body from the observation (None clears holding).

The belief-side simulator (env.sim_world, SceneBelief.world) is built by setup_world with the TRUE scene poses for all objects including the die; set_sim only repositions objects in object_poses, so the hidden die stays at its true pose in the belief client for the whole episode. look_sample_fn reads pbu.get_pose(look_at_obj) from b0.world (true die pose when ?o is the die), look_effects_fn renders depth in that client, and plan_motion/grasp_ik treat all environment bodies there (die included) as obstacles.
facts.evidence: env.py:842-848 (sim_world), 683-699 (setup_world set_pose), 135-140 (set_sim), 612-617 (look_sample_fn get_pose), 474-485 (look_effects_fn render), 340-347 and 383-388 (obstacles = world.environment)

facts.claim: ActionSchema pick(?o physical, ?g grasp): preconditions Not(moved ?o), Not(Exists holding), known-pose ?o, object-grasp ?o ?g; effects Not(at-home); verify_effects holding ?o, at-grasp ?o ?g. Each object can be picked at most once per episode because place adds moved(?o).

ActionSchema place(?o, ?g, ?p pose): preconditions holding ?o, at-grasp ?o ?g, object-pose ?o ?p; effects moved ?o, Not(at-home), Not(holding ?o), Not(at-grasp ?o ?g), known-pose ?o; no verify_effects (deterministic in the symbolic model).

ActionSchema look(?o1, ?o2, ?q conf) = 'looking behind ?o2 for ?o1': depends [moved ?o2]; preconditions looking-conf ?o2 ?q, Not(known-pose ?o1), known-pose ?o2, Not(Exists holding); effects Not(at-home); verify_effects known-pose ?o1. 'moved ?o2' is NOT a precondition, only a depends (conditions the learned outcome statistics via closed_fluents), so looks at unmoved cups are legal.
ActionSchema go-home(): preconditions Exists holding, Not(at-home); effects at-home; no verify_effects. NoOp() is in the action list with empty preconditions and identity effects.

Reward/goal = And([Exists ?o physical. And(is-target ?o, holding ?o), at-home]); get_reward evaluates it with eval_expr on abstract_belief.items + store.certified and returns float(bool). Success is a belief predicate, never a physical-state check.

Streams: look-conf-sample(?o physical) -> ?q conf certifying looking-conf(?o,?q); grasp-sample(?o) -> ?g certifying object-grasp(?o,?g); place-sample(?o) -> ?p certifying object-pose(?o,?p). With flat_sample true, TampuraPolicy calls flat_stream_sample(times = flat_width = 5) ONLY at the first replan (self.sampled latch), for every typed object combination including the die, so all continuous values of an episode are fixed at t=0.

look_sample_fn: camera target = object pose at sample time offset by N(0,0.1) in x,y and U(0.2,0.3) in z, oriented to look at the object; converted to a gripper pose via the current camera_T_gripper; IK through plan_workspace_motion with obstacles=[floor] only; up to 100 attempts; returns the first arm configuration. Because sampling happens at t=0, look confs for a cup point at the cup's ORIGINAL location.

grasp_sample_fn uses get_grasp(..., grasp_mode='saved'): loads every JSON under <mesh dir>/grasps/, shuffles, and returns the first grasp whose open gripper does not collide with the object and whose close_until_collision finds a contact; closed_position scaled by 1.05. The grasp library lives in models/srl/ycb/<object>/grasps/*.json (precompute_grasps.py writes {'grasp': tool_from_grasp}), which is NOT in the Windows mirrors (MODELS_LISTING only).

place_sample_fn samples uniformly over a 'shortened table' (centre (0.475, 0, -0.015), 0.75 x 1.22 x 0.015) shrunk by the object's half extents, random yaw, z = 0.0075 + object half height + 0.01 (object bottom about 2.5 mm above the real table top); there is NO collision check against other objects or the die.

pick_effects_fn: set_sim, then grasp_ik(world, obj, belief pose, grasp, obstacles = environment minus obj plus floor); success iff a pregrasp->grasp workspace path exists; the successor belief carries grasp=grasp. pick_execute_fn: same grasp_ik, then plan_motion (BiRRT) from belief.current_conf to the pregrasp conf; on either failure returns the unchanged state and an observation without grasp (belief stays not holding); on success runs pick_execute and sets obs.grasp, obs.grasp_body, obs.conf = pregrasp conf.

place_effects_fn: grasp_ik at the placement pose; successor observation sets moved=o, poses={o: placement_pose}. place_execute_fn: ik(world, obj, p, g) (floor-only obstacles) then plan_motion with attachments=[grasp_attachment]; on failure returns state and an observation that KEEPS the grasp (still holding); on success obs.poses[obj] = commanded placement (not observed), grasp cleared, moved set.

look_effects_fn: set_sim, set arm joints to q in the belief client, render depth, new_seen = voxels freed by this image; outcomes: fail belief (image applied) with count = occupied - len(new_seen), success belief with count = len(new_seen) whose object_poses[?o1] = Pose(random newly seen voxel centre) and current_conf None. look_execute_fn: plan_motion to q (obstacles floor + environment), apply, render in the REAL world, obs_from_camera_image (true poses of visible bodies), obs.conf = q.

home_effects_fn and home_execute_fn both construct the observation with conf = DEFAULT_ARM_POS before planning; home_execute_fn returns that observation unchanged when plan_motion returns None, so the belief records at-home even if the arm never moved. go-home therefore cannot fail from the belief's (and the reward's) point of view.

Execution is kinematic: SceneState.apply_sequence iterates GroupTrajectory.iterate; with teleport=True (chosen as not has_gui) it sets joints to the last waypoint; with a GUI it steps an interpolated curve via set_joint_positions (resetJointState) with time.sleep(5e-3) per iterate; sim_steps defaults to 0 so stepSimulation is never called; the held object is kept at the tool by enforce_grasp -> Attachment.assign -> set_pose (resetBasePositionAndOrientation) each iterate. No createConstraint anywhere in the pick/place path.

pick_execute: move along the BiRRT plan, approach along the pregrasp path, close the gripper by linspace from OPEN_GRIPPER_POS [0.045,0.045] to grasp.closed_position (GRIPPER_RES 1 mm), set state.grasp, retreat along the reversed pregrasp path. place_execute: move, approach, open to OPEN_GRIPPER_POS, state.grasp = None, retreat. Objects released kinematically stay where set (no gravity step).

Motion planning: plan_motion_fn -> plan_joint_motion -> birrt (motion_planners/rrt_connect.py) with resolutions 10 degrees, restarts 1, iterations 20, smooth 100, max_iterations 1000, max_distance COLLISION_DISTANCE 5e-3, self_collisions True; collision_fn checks joint limits, self link pairs and moving links (plus attachments) against obstacles. DISABLE_ALL_COLLISIONS=True is passed as disable_collisions but get_collision_fn never reads it (swallowed by **kwargs), so obstacle collisions ARE checked; in plan_workspace_motion the same flag only skips the post-IK pairwise_collisions re-check.

Panda model constants: PANDA_PATH = models/srl/franka_panda/panda.urdf; ARM_GROUP joints panda_joint1..7; GRIPPER_GROUP panda_finger_joint1/2; PANDA_TOOL_TIP 'panda_tool_tip'; CAMERA_FRAME 'camera_frame'; DEFAULT_ARM_POS = [-0.0806, -1.6723, 0.0707, -2.7449, 0.0818, 1.7516, 0.7849]; OPEN 0.045 per finger, CLOSE 0; robot loaded with fixed_base=True in a bc.BulletClient (GUI iff vis, GUI panel and shadows off). The urdf itself is not in any local mirror.

PAPER_AUDIT.txt #P5 records (from the archived bridge) that their Panda's EE frame is panda_grasptarget link 14 and finger links are 12 and 13 versus ours 11 and [9,10]; this is not verifiable from the mirrored sources (urdf absent) and conflicts in name with PANDA_TOOL_TIP = 'panda_tool_tip' used by the code.

Two PyBullet clients per episode: setup_robot(vis) for the real world and setup_robot(vis=False, camera_matrix=...) for the belief world; both built by setup_world in identical order (table, posts, beams, then objects in category order) so body ids coincide; World.client resolves through the module-level CLIENT_MAP[client_id] (keeps World picklable). TampuraEnv exposes env.state (SceneState: world, grasp), env.world, env.sim_world, env.starting_belief, env.problem_spec (lru_cached), env.vis.

Policy.rollout: asserts problem_spec.verify(store); saves config.yml; for step in range(max_steps): s = deepcopy(env.state); a_b = b.abstract(store); reward = get_reward(a_b); action, info, store = self.get_action(b, store); if action.name == 'no-op': bp = deepcopy(b), observation None; else observation = env.step(action, b, store); bp = b.update(action, observation, store); history.add(..., time.time()-st); b = bp. After the loop a final record (len = max_steps + 1), env.wrapup(), pickle to save_dir/<datetime>.pkl.

A custom policy = subclass of Policy with get_action(belief, store) -> (Action(name, args), info, store) where args are store symbol strings (e.g. 'o_ph_0', 'o_gr_3', 'o_po_6', 'o_co_8'; add_typed names them f'o_{type[:2]}_{counter}'); registration via tampura.config.config.register_planner(id, cls) and config 'planner: id'; run_planner.py only imports tampura and tampura_environments, so a wrapper entry point (or import hook) is needed to register a new policy. New continuous values can be added through problem_spec.flat_stream_sample, execute_stream_plan, or store.add_typed + store.certified.append(Atom(...)).
facts.evidence: policy.py:93-94; random_policy.py:10-29; policies/__init__.py:12-18; config.py:47-52; store.py:59-63, 69-82; spec.py:102-138; policy_search.py:205-228; run_planner.py:11-14, 135-137

facts.claim: applicable_actions grounds each schema's preconditions over store.type_dict and abstract_belief.items + store.certified and drops actions whose symbols resolve to None in the store; TampuraPolicy falls back to a random applicable action when the MDP's choice is not applicable, and to no-op when F has no effects.

TampuraPolicy.get_action: if reward(ab) > 0 return no-op; compute envelope_prob as the product of F probabilities along the executed (ab, a) chain; if envelope_prob < envelope_threshold (1): with from_scratch reset F, R, belief_map; flat-sample streams once; run policy_search in batches of batch_size until num_samples; then solve_mdp (value iteration, mdptoolbox, gamma) and pick sol.policy[ab]. With envelope_prob >= 1 no new sampling happens and the old F is reused.

policy_search per batch: write PDDL (domain with one deterministic action per verify-effect outcome combo, costs from Bayes-optimistic beta quantiles injected into the SAS file), run SymK translate and search (python fast-downward.py, search time limit 20 s, symk-fw, num_plans = num_skeletons) via subprocess, convert plans to abstract rollouts, then for batch_size steps pick the least-sampled transition of a random rollout and call action_schema.effects_fn(action, random belief in belief_map[ab], store) to grow F. SymK output is parsed from sas_plan* files.

RolloutHistory.time_deltas[i] = time.time() - st at history.add after step i (cumulative since rollout start); per-step planning time is the difference of consecutive entries. The sweep's loop_s = time_deltas[-1]; wall_s = subprocess wall clock; symk_solve_s = sum of 'Time:' lines parsed from stdout (0.04 to 1.5 s per episode); success = rewards[-1] == 1.0; solve_step = first index with reward 1.0 (reward at the START of that step).

Local 20-seed run (2026-05-26, seeds 0-19, per-episode timeout 900 s, none hit, all return code 0, all 20 actions per episode): 11/20 success (seeds 0,2,4,6,7,9,11,12,13,17,19); loop_s all 239.9 +/- 151.1 s (min 81.8, max 728.9), successes 166.1 +/- 84.7 s; wall_s all 253.3 +/- 150.9 s; solve_step for successes 5,5,11,6,6,6,6,7,6,11,15. Output dirs runs/run_<time>/ in WSL hold config.yml, logs/, pddl_t=*_s=*/ and a RolloutHistory pickle.

Observed per-step costs: seed 0 (2-object scene) outcome sampling took 58 s at t=0 and 10 s at t=4, total loop 81.8 s; seed 1 (5-object scene) 96 s and 85 s for the first two replans; seed 18's resumed run 153 s for one replan. SymK search itself is 12 to 40 ms per call.

Failure mode of the inspected failures: after a look that reveals nothing, the policy repeats the identical look action to step 20 without any 'Flat Action Parameter Sampling'/'Outcome Sampling' lines (seed 1: look(o_ph_0, o_ph_4, o_co_14) x16 from t=4; seed 16: look(o_ph_1, o_ph_0, o_co_2) x19 from t=1; seed 18: look(o_ph_0, o_ph_3, o_co_3) repeated). Mechanism: F holds a probability-1 self-loop for that look, so envelope_prob = 1 >= envelope_threshold suppresses replanning and the MDP re-selects it. These are policy-loop failures, not physical failures.
facts.evidence: seed_1.log:79-110 and grep lines 93-275; seed_16.log:17-269; seed_18.log:91-239; tampura_policy.py:83-99

facts.claim: A successful episode (seed 19, 5-object scene, die under e_cups_ud = o_ph_2) shows the intended loop: pick/place a cup, look behind it, repeat for four cups, then pick the die (o_ph_3) and go-home at t=14, reward 1.0 from t=15, no-ops to t=19. seed 0 (2-object scene) solves in 5 actions: pick cup, place, look, pick die, go-home.

Object creation: create_ycb loads google_16k/textured.obj (visual) and textured_vhacd.obj (collision) from models/srl/ycb/<name>/, centred at the mesh centre of mass, createMultiBody with baseMass=-1 (pybullet default mass) and white colour. The table is a static box (STATIC_MASS 0) with lateral friction 1.0; posts and beams are created but not in the obstacle list.

The tampura library's policies registry: random_policy, uct_policy, tabular_q_learning, tampura_policy, replay_policy, dqn_policy, contingent_policy. The 'load' config path replays a saved RolloutHistory (store taken from execution_data.stores[-1]).

The local TAMPURA install is WSL /root/tampura-work (tampura + tampura_environments cloned depth 1 from aidan-curtis GitHub, python3.11 venv, SymK built from third_party/symk, pybullet 3.2.7); SymK shells out to bare 'python', so the venv bin must be on PATH; the GUI launcher runs run_planner.py --config=./env_configs/find_dice.yml --vis=1 --global-seed=SEED --vis-graph=1 from the tampura_environments directory (cwd matters: the problems path is relative).
The paper reference values recorded by the sweep driver (planning 57 +/- 38 s, success >= 0.63, 20 seeds) are copied from Curtis et al. 2024 and were not verified in this read.

design_relevant_details: Entry point to reuse unchanged: run_planner.py flow = tconfig.load_config(yml, cli) -> random.seed/np.random.seed(global_seed) -> setup_logger(save_dir) -> env = get_env('find_dice')(config=config) -> b0, store = env.initialize() -> policy = get_planner(name)(config, env.problem_spec, execution_data=None) -> policy.rollout(env, b0, store). A bridge policy must be registered (register_planner) before get_planner, so the bridge needs its own thin entry script in OUR repo that imports our policy module and then performs the same sequence (or imports run_planner's logic); their files stay untouched.

Policy contract: class X(Policy): get_action(self, belief: SceneBelief, store: AliasStore) -> Tuple[Action, Dict, AliasStore]; Action(name in {'pick','place','look','go-home','no-op'}, args = list of store symbols). Their executor runs only for non-no-op actions (env.step -> schema.execute_fn). The returned store is carried forward; info is stored in history.infos.

Store symbols: add_typed(value, type) names 'o_<type[:2]>_<n>' (physical -> o_ph_n = body id; grasp -> o_gr_n = Grasp object with .grasp tool_from_grasp pose, .pregrasp, .closed_position; pose -> o_po_n = (point, quat); conf -> o_co_n = 7-tuple). Certified facts live in store.certified as Atom('looking-conf'|'object-grasp'|'object-pose', [...]). Any new continuous value our policy wants their executor to use must be added this way (e.g. store.add_typed(conf, 'conf') + Atom('looking-conf', [o2, q])).

Belief handles available to a policy: belief.object_poses (known poses), belief.visibility_grid (VoxelGrid: .occupied list of (i,j,k), .center_from_voxel, .to_world, .aabb, resolutions 0.015), belief.current_conf, belief.grasp/grasp_body, belief.moved, belief.world (World: .client BulletClient, .robot PandaRobot(.body int), .objects body ids, .categories, .floor, .environment). env.state.world is the REAL client. Body ids coincide across clients.

Camera: wrist link 'camera_frame'; matrix [[525,0,319.5],[0,525,239.5],[0,0,1]], 640x480, far 5.0, segmentation mask [:,:,0] = body id. The initial sense is at DEFAULT_ARM_POS. A 'fixed camera' for our shadow model can only be the wrist camera pose at DEFAULT_ARM_POS (or at a planned look conf).

Hidden-object belief in their model: uniform over surviving 15 mm voxels in a 2-layer slab (z about 0.01 to 0.04 m) over x in [0.37, 0.815], y in [-0.61, 0.61]. The die in two of three scenes floats at z about 0.05 inside the inverted cup; after a physics step it would drop to the table inside the cup.

Success predicate (theirs, binding for the comparison): Exists o: is-target(o) & holding(o) & at-home on the abstract belief; holding requires an observation with grasp set (only pick_execute_fn sets it, iff IK + BiRRT succeed); at-home requires belief.current_conf allclose DEFAULT_ARM_POS (go-home's observation sets it unconditionally).

Episode shape: exactly max_steps = 20 get_action calls; the history has 21 reward entries; success = rewards[-1] == 1.0; no-op after goal. loop time = time_deltas[-1]. For a fair timing comparison use per-step deltas and/or time to first reward 1.0, and run both systems headless (their GUI path sleeps 5 ms per interpolation step).

Their action set is bounded: pick requires Not(moved ?o), so each cup can be relocated once; look is only parameterised by (target, reference object, conf); the die identity is given (is-target) and the goal is to hold it at home, not to place it.
Streams are frozen at t=0 (flat_width 5): 5 grasps, 5 placements, 5 look confs per object. Placements have no inter-object collision check; look confs aim at each object's t=0 pose.

Execution semantics to match or to replace: kinematic teleport in headless mode; Attachment.assign = set_pose of the carried object; no stepSimulation; BiRRT (rrt_connect) with 5 mm clearance against table + all objects; grasp library from models/srl/ycb/<obj>/grasps/*.json (not mirrored on Windows, present in WSL /root/tampura-work/tampura_environments/models).

Seed pinning: record scene file per seed from the 'Loading scene from' console line; mapping on the WSL tree: 1747173590 <- {1,2,3,4,8,14,15,18}, 1747173591 <- {0,7,9,11,12,13,16}, 1747173593 <- {5,6,10,17,19}. os.listdir order is not guaranteed elsewhere.

Config knobs that must stay identical for TAMPURA's own arm of the comparison: find_dice.yml as snapshotted in sweep_2026-05-26.json env_config_snapshot (max_steps 20, num_samples 200, batch 20, skeletons 10, flat_width 5, gamma 0.98, envelope_threshold 1, from_scratch true).

Output artefacts per episode: runs/run_<time>/config.yml, logs/<time>.log (all print_options), pddl_t=<t>_s=<n>/{domain.pddl, problem.pddl, output.sas, sas_plan*}, <datetime>.pkl (RolloutHistory with states, beliefs, abstract_beliefs, actions, observations, rewards, time_deltas, stores, infos).

Unfairness inventory to disclose in the plan (either direction): (1) hand-tuned reachable spawns and camera-visibility-checked scenes, only 3 scenes; (2) perfect segmentation-gated pose perception; (3) kinematic execution: picks cannot physically fail, nothing falls, placements may interpenetrate; (4) belief-judged success and go-home that always believes at-home; (5) saved grasp library validated by close-until-collision; (6) hidden die present at true pose in the belief simulator (affects their look-conf sampler, renders and collision checks); (7) no early termination and envelope-loop failures that burn steps; (8) their per-step time is dominated by 200 effects_fn samples (IK/BiRRT/render), ours by PDDLStream; (9) headless teleport vs GUI interpolation changes wall time.
honesty_risks: Reading the die's pose from either PyBullet client (belief.world or env.state.world) before it has been observed: the die body sits at its TRUE pose in the belief-side simulator for the whole episode (env.py:842-848 vs 135-140), and world.poses are ground truth. Any bridge perception must be gated by a rendered segmentation/depth image exactly as obs_from_camera_image is, and never by body id lookup of the target.

Constructing SceneObservation objects ourselves (poses, grasp, conf, moved) if the bridge bypasses their execute_fn: this is where 'their belief internals written as truth' happens. If we write obs.grasp without a physical hold check we re-create the CB#123 flaw; if we write obs.poses from get_pose we create an oracle. Prefer either (a) emitting their Action objects so their executor produces the observation, or (b) a documented perception adapter that only reads the rendered image.

Using store symbols that encode scene knowledge (e.g. choosing 'o_ph_3' because the logs show the die is under d_cups_ud in scene 1747173590): the bridge must derive every pick/look target from the belief and the planner, never from the scene JSON or the console logs (H4).

Letting the bridge pick the cup order by a fixed heuristic (nearest, largest, left-to-right) outside the planner: this is exactly the discarded bridge's failure. The order must come from the PDDLStream plan over Know-If / containment-region fluents.

Accepting their kinematic carry (Attachment.assign = resetBasePositionAndOrientation) as 'physics' for OUR arm of the comparison: if our policy drives their executors (option a), the comparison is of planners under THEIR kinematic executor and must be labelled so; if we execute with physics inside their client (option b), the die in two scenes will drop from cup height when physics steps and the inverted cups may react, which changes the scene relative to TAMPURA's arm and must be recorded.

Treating go-home as succeeded on no_path: their own env does this (env.py:563-581); mirroring it in our execution would inflate our success the same way. Our arm must thread the real status and count go-home no_path as failure, and the write-up must state that TAMPURA's reported success does not have this check.

Comparing wall time across different step semantics: theirs always runs 20 steps with no-ops after the goal and includes 200 effects_fn samples per replan; a per-episode total is not comparable to our time-to-goal. Report time to first reward 1.0 (from time_deltas) and per-step planning time, both headless.

Seed-for-seed claims that silently use a different seed-to-scene map: random.choice(os.listdir(...)) depends on directory order. Pin scene files per seed from the logs and assert the loaded scene in our runs; otherwise 'same seeds' is not 'same scenes'.

Editing anything under their tree (env.py precondition tweaks, a 'moved' precondition on look, a goal change, visibility AABB) to make our side work: H4 forbids it; all adaptation lives in our repo. Note that their look does NOT require the reference cup to have moved, so an apples-to-apples action set on our side must not add that precondition silently.

Using their saved grasp library or their look-conf sampler as a 'better sampler' without recording it as a model change: those are their continuous parameter sources; if adopted, each is an audit entry with before/after (ties to #P5).
open_questions: Which bridge mode does the plan commit to: (a) our policy emits THEIR Action schema instances and their execute_fn/observation/belief/reward run untouched (cleanest honesty, but our arm then inherits their kinematic executor and belief-judged success), or (b) our own physics execution inside their real client with a documented image-gated perception adapter producing SceneObservation (closer to our thesis pipeline, but observation construction is on our side and must be audited)? The archived #P4 note calls (a)-style native action execution 'optional extra faithfulness'.

How does our fixed-camera shadow model map onto their wrist camera: is the fixed camera defined as the camera_frame pose at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, with sense = go-home + render, and is a 'look conf' action (their look) in scope or out of scope for our side?

Containment regions: the die hypothesis in their model is the cup cavity footprint; our lateral shadows never cover it. The planned 'look underneath a certain kind of object' tweak needs a region type (cup footprint / under-object volume) and a Know-If fluent; which object classes qualify (all *_cups_ud? any object with a cavity detectable from the mesh? any object at all, as 'under' volume)?

Physics in their client: do we step physics (letting the floating die in scenes 1747173591/1747173593 drop into the cup) and record it as a scene-level difference, or do we keep their no-physics world for both arms?

The actual Panda urdf link indices (PAPER_AUDIT #P5 says EE link 14 'panda_grasptarget', fingers 12/13) cannot be verified from the mirrors; the urdf must be read from WSL /root/tampura-work/tampura_environments/models/srl/franka_panda/panda.urdf before any IK code is written.

Timing baseline: should TAMPURA's arm be re-run alongside ours on the same machine state (the 2026-05-26 run predates several host changes), and should its per-step time_deltas be extracted from the pickles rather than only loop_s?

Whether the envelope-loop degeneracy in TAMPURA's failures (seeds 1, 16, 18) should be reported as a TAMPURA policy artefact in the paper, given it accounts for all inspected failures in the local run.

Do the three shipped scenes suffice for a 20-seed comparison (only 3 distinct scenes, repeated 8/7/5 times with different stream samples), or should the plan include running env_generator.py offline to produce more scenes, which would no longer be 'their exact seeds' (H4) and must then be a separate, clearly labelled experiment?
